entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Shailendra Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
Heard Sri Shailendra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rohit Dubey, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 263 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 of IPC, Police Station Robertsganj, District Sonbhadra, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

As per prosecution story, the applicant and one unknown person are stated to have invested an amount of Rs.36,000/- and Rs.72,000/- from the informant and his wife on 02.09.2013 on the pretext that it shall double the amount to Rs.1,16,000/- after a period of six years i.e. on 02.09.2019.

The applicant is stated to have refused to return the said amount to the informant and his wife as such, he has usurped the said amount.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive.
The applicant is just an agent in the company and he himself invested his hard earned money in the name of his wife and sister-in-law in it, as such, he himself is a victim.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that the applicant was simply an agent in the company and also the fact that he has no criminal history.

On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.
